newsitem.title: UK: Patten says Tory leader bid "extremely unlikely".
newsitem.headline: Patten says Tory leader bid "extremely unlikely".

text.p: Hong Kong governor Chris Patten said it was "extremely unlikely" that he would be a candidate for the leadership of the British Conservative Party when he finishes his term in the British colony.
Patten, a former chairman of the Conservative Party, is often mentioned as a possible candidate as next party leader should John Major should step down.
But he told BBC television in an interview on Friday that he had not even decided whether he wanted to try to get elected as a member of parliament in Britain again.

"While I know that I want to do something in public services I don't really know whether I'm determined on the task of getting back to Westminister," said Patten, whose job as governor ends on June 30, 1997 when Hong Kong is returned to China.

"I think it would be ludicrous for me after nearly five years away from British politics...to start talking about whether or not I...should be a candidate for the future leadership of the Conservative Party, it seems to me extremely unlikely that will ever happen," he said.
